= Glasgow Surname Y-DNA Project =

This is the project's current guide to Y-DNA evidence for Glasgow and variant-surname paternal lines. Y-DNA can identify paternal clusters, test whether two documented male lines share a male ancestor and estimate when a branch formed. It cannot by itself name that ancestor, select between same-name historical men or repair a missing documentary generation.

== Primary project resources ==

* [https://www.familytreedna.com/groups/glasgow/ FamilyTreeDNA Glasgow Surname Group] — project membership and testing information.
* [https://www.familytreedna.com/public/Glasgow?iframe=ysnp Public Y-DNA SNP results] and [https://www.familytreedna.com/public/Glasgow?iframe=yresults public STR results] — the current testing-platform data.
* [https://groups.io/g/glasgowdnaproject Glasgow DNA Project discussion group] — questions, coordination and project updates.
* [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/ydna Glasgow Y-DNA Explorer] and [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/timeline Y-DNA Timeline] — project visualisations. These are finding aids; platform results and documentary sources remain the evidence.

== How to use the evidence ==

# Build each tester's direct male-line pedigree from cited birth, marriage, death, probate, census and other relationship records.
# Record the earliest reliably documented paternal ancestor and the exact uncertainty in each link.
# Compare Y-DNA only after the documentary lines have been separated.
# Use Big Y SNP results to define branches; use STRs for screening and project grouping, not as proof of a named ancestor.
# Report genetic dates as estimates and include the displayed uncertainty interval where available.
# Keep a historical identification labelled as a hypothesis until a documentary bridge or ancient-DNA comparison tests it.

== Project topology ==

The principal working path is:

:R-M269 → R-U106 → R-Z18 → R-Z17 → [[Space:R-S20045|R-S20045]] → [[Space:R-S14827|R-S14827]] → [[Space:R-FT4811|R-FT4811]] → [[Space:R-FT32941|R-FT32941]] → [[Space:R-FT25406|R-FT25406]]

Relevant downstream or comparison pages include [[Space:R-FT20271|R-FT20271]], [[Space:R-FTA30932|R-FTA30932]] and [[Space:R-BY136156|R-BY136156]]. The individual SNP pages record platform-derived topology, estimates and branch-specific notes. Their historical narratives must follow the same evidence rules as this page.

== Relationship to the documentary study ==

The [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Bearers_of_the_%27%27de_Glasgu%27%27_Name_and_the_Emergence_of_the_Glasgow_Surname%2C_c.1175%E2%80%931500 pre-1500 register] documents people who used ''de Glasgu'' and related forms. [[Space:Glasgow Branches in 15th and 16th Century Scotland|Early Scottish branches]] establishes the first secure multi-generation burgh pedigree. [[Space:Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland|Early Ireland]] separates Irish record clusters.

No current evidence joins a tested modern male line continuously to a named pre-1500 bearer. The correct research target is therefore the missing documentary bridge, not the retrospective assignment of medieval people to modern SNPs.

== Paternal pedigree matrix ==

This matrix deliberately reports branches rather than private tester identities. A branch is ready for a historical conclusion only when each tester-to-root generation has independently cited relationship evidence.

== Testing and research priorities ==

* recruit patrilineal descendants of independently documented Scottish, Irish and diaspora root families;
* upgrade representative lines to Big Y where appropriate;
* resolve the documentary pedigree of every kit before drawing branch conclusions;
* seek tests from lines not expected to belong to R-FT25406, so non-paternity, surname adoption and multiple surname origins remain visible;
* update the WikiTree SNP pages when the testing platform changes topology or estimates;
* publish anonymised conclusions only, respecting each tester's consent and privacy.
